new_statements.rule_in_words: Beiya (the main Gəmnəm/Gimnime lect) is described as a tonal language; no statement about word stress or accent is made in any accessible source. Second-hand (Fabre 2020: 135, summarising Dieu's sketch in the 2016 dictionary): 'Sur le plan tonal, les auteurs mentionnent trois tons ponctuels et deux tons modulés' = three level tones and two contour tones; again nothing on stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is a one-sentence typological profile in a morphosyntax working paper by a fieldworker on Beiya; the only dedicated phonological sketch (Dieu in Dieu & Perrois 2016, 3 pp.) was not accessible and could contain an accent remark.
new_statements.identity_note: All accessible first-hand material is on the Beiya lect (with Gindoo and Riitime) of Gəmnəm/Gəmnəme, which Kleinewillinghöfer 2015 and Littig 2020 equate with Gimnime [gmn, gimn1238]; Dieu & Perrois's 'koma gɨ́mbē' is the same language (Boyd 1989: 'the Gɨmbe speaking Gɨmnɨme'; Glottolog files the dictionary under gimn1238). Not to be confused with the sister language Gimme/Kompana/Panme [kmp, gimm1239] or the northern 'Koma' lects (Gəunəm, Vɔmnəm, Damtəm), which are Vere-group.

tone_statements.quote: My assistants in Gəmme and Beiya were trained in writing their language in orthographies developed by Lutheran Bible translators based at Ngaoundere, especially by Lars Lode. Both orthographies mark tone. [...] For all other languages, the transcriptions attempt to represent the sounds and tones phonemically, biased towards orthographies for local uses. High tones and clear low tones are marked; mid-tones are generally unmarked, unless where ambiguity may arise, e.g. when a mid-tone follows/precedes a high or low tone in a CVV or CVC2 structure.

No mention of stress/accent.

sources.note: No tonal analysis, but a first-hand transcription statement: the Beiya (and Gəmme) practical orthographies developed by Lutheran Bible translators (Lars Lode, Ngaoundéré) mark tone; the author's own transcriptions of Beiya/Riitime etc. mark high and 'clear low' tones and leave mid tones unmarked except where ambiguous, i.e. a three-height (H/M/L) surface marking; all Beiya and Riitime noun-class data are tone-marked. Consistent with the 3 level + 2 contour tones reported second-hand for Koma gɨ́mbē (Fabre 2020 on Dieu & Perrois 2016).
sources.venue: Klassensprachen des Samba-Duru am oberen Benue und ihre Beziehungen zum Gur
